STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r3.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r3.claim: Āl also includes verse 197 among the Madinan verses.
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r3.anchor: others include v. 197 among the Madinan verses (Āl).

STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r11.claim: The Quran is revealed in Arabic to a people meant to understand and comprehend it.
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r11.anchor: it was revealed in Arabic to a people who are meant to understand and comprehend it (vv. 197–200)

ASAD-NOTES:26:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:intro/r2.claim: Asad rejects Suyuti’s Medina dating of 26:197 based only on its mention of Israelite scholars, since such references also occur in Meccan revelations.
ASAD-NOTES:26:intro/r2.anchor: as Suyuti does, that verse 197 belongs to the Medina period

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.claim: The concluding discourse returns to the sūrah's opening theme: Qur'anic warnings are true, punishment signs can come, and prophetic histories already serve as signs for the stubborn Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.anchor: Coming up are the concluding verses of the sūrah and the discourse links to its introductory part which is the real theme.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r1.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits that Meccans consulted Yathrib's Jewish scholars about the Prophet, who described his time and traits but became confused about Muhammad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r1.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي، عن ابن عباس، أن أهل مكة بعثوا إلى أحبار يثرب يسألونهم عن النبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r2.claim: The revelation's Meccan setting supports this report; Muqātil instead says the verse is Medinan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r2.anchor: ويؤيد هذا كون الآية مكية. وقال مقاتل: هي مدنية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r3.claim: They identify Israel's scholars as converts such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who pointed to passages in Torah and Gospel about the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r3.anchor: وعلماء بني إسرائيل: عبد الله بن سلام ونحوه، قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r4.claim: Other interpretations include all Israelite scholars, whether converted or not, and their prophets who foretold the Messenger's traits, time, and place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: علماؤهم من أسلم منهم ومن لم يسلم. وقيل: أنبياؤهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r5.claim: The majority read a masculine verb and accusative āyatan, with the infinitive clause as the subject of yakun and āya between the two.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أولم يكن، بالياء من تحت، آية: بالنصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r6.speaker: ابن عامر والجحدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r6.claim: They read takun with feminine agreement and nominative āyatun; al-Zamakhsharī finds the indefinite subject and definite predicate awkward and offers a clause or story-pronoun parse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر، والجحدري: تكن بالتاء من فوق، آية: بالرفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r7.claim: He reads the feminine verb with accusative āyatan; Abū Ḥayyān compares feminine agreement based on the predicate or an interpreted feminine noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس: تكن بالتاء من فوق، آية بالنصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r8.speaker: الجحدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r8.claim: He reads an taʿlamahu with feminine agreement, supported by a line in which Banū ʿĀmir is paired with a feminine verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري: أن تعلمه بتاء التأنيث، كما قال الشاعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r9.claim: The Medinan codex spells ʿalimū with waw, reflecting a dialect that shifts final alif toward wāw, as in prayer, alms, and usury spellings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189#2/r9.anchor: وكتب في المصحف: علموا بواو بين الميم والألف. قيل: على لغة من يميل ألف علموا

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads takun with feminine tāʾ and āyatun in the nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر " تكن " بالتاء من فوق " آية " بالرفع

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r2.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r2.claim: The other readers use masculine yakun and āyatan in the accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r2.anchor: والباقون " يكن " بالياء من تحت " آية " بالنصب

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads feminine takun with āyatan in the accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r3.anchor: وابن عباس " تكن " بالتاء من فوق و " آية " بالنصب

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r4.claim: For Ibn ʿĀmir's reading, takūnu may be a complete verb: lahum attaches to it and āya is its subject; an yaʿlamahu is either apposition to āya or a predicate of an omitted subject.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r4.anchor: فأما قراءة ابن عامر ف " تكون " تحتمل أن تكون تامة

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r5.claim: On an incomplete-verb parse, one option makes the subject the pronoun of the matter and the following clause its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r5.anchor: أحدها: أن يكون اسمها مضمرا فيها بمعنى القصة

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r6.claim: A second incomplete parse makes the matter-pronoun its subject, lahum its fronted predicate, and āya its delayed subject; an yaʿlamahu is apposition or a predicate of an omitted subject.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r6.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون اسمها ضمير القصة أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r7.claim: A third incomplete parse makes lahum the fronted predicate of takun and āya its subject; an yaʿlamahu is again apposition or a predicate of an omitted subject.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r7.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون " لهم " خبر " تكن " مقدما

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r8.claim: A fourth parse makes āya the subject and an yaʿlamahu its predicate, but objections call the indefinite subject before a definite predicate poetic necessity; al-Samīn rejects that defense and says there is no need for this parse.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r8.anchor: ولا ضرورة تدعو إلى هذا التخريج، بل التخريج ما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r9.claim: For the other readers, āyatan is a fronted predicate, an yaʿlamahu the delayed subject, and lahum attaches circumstantially to āya.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r9.anchor: وأما قراءة الباقين فواضحة جدا ف " آية " خبر مقدم

SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's agreement pattern parallels the cited verse and poetry: a feminine verb can agree with a feminine predicate or a verbal noun understood as feminine.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197/r10.anchor: وأما قراءة ابن عباس فكقراءة { ثم لم تكن فتنتهم إلا أن قالوا }

SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r1.speaker: الجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r1.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads an taʿlamahu with feminine tāʾ, treating Banū Isrāʾīl, a broken plural, as a feminine singular for agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري: " أن تعلمه " بالتاء من فوق

SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r2.claim: A cited line uses feminine singular qālat with the tribe name Banū ʿĀmir, providing a poetic parallel for the agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r2.anchor: قالت بنو عامر خالوا بني أسد يا بؤس للجهل

SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r3.claim: The written rasm has a wāw after the mīm plus alif; one explanation is a dialect that inclines alif toward wāw, as in ṣalāh and zakāh.
SAMIN-DURR:26:197#2/r3.anchor: وكتبوا في الرسم الكريم " علمؤا " بواو الميم والألف

ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n84/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n84/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n84/r1.claim: The people for whom this is evidence are those who disbelieve in Muhammad's prophethood.
ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n84/r1.anchor: I.e., for those who disbelieve in the prophethood of Muhammad.

ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n85/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n85/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n85/r1.claim: The learned Israelites include Jewish converts such as 'Abd Allah ibn Salim and Ka'b ibn Malik in Medina in the Prophet's lifetime, Ka'b al-Ahbar and Yemenite peers under 'Umar, and later converts.
ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n85/r1.anchor: for instance, 'Abd Allah ibn Salim, Ka'b ibn Malik and other learned Jews of Medina in the lifetime of the Prophet

ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n85/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n85/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n85/r2.claim: Only learned Jews are named because the Torah survives in corrupted form, whereas Jesus's original revelation has been lost and cannot attest to the shared fundamentals of his teaching and the Qur'an.
ASAD-NOTES:26:197#n85/r2.anchor: contrary to the Torah, which still exists, albeit in a corrupted form - the original revelation granted to Jesus has been lost

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r1.claim: Ibn Amir alone reads the verb with feminine tāʾ and makes āya nominative; all others use the masculine verb with āya accusative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r1.anchor: وكلهم قرأ: أولم يكن لهم آية [الشعراء/ 197] نصبا، غير ابن عامر فإنه قرأ: (تكن) بالتاء (آية) بالرفع

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r2.claim: For Ibn Amir's reading, تكن may refer to an implicit story or report; آية is then predicate of أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل. Feminine agreement can follow a feminine noun inside the explanatory clause, as in the cited examples.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: وجه قول ابن عامر: (تكن لهم آية) أن (تكن) ليس للآية

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r3.claim: Alternatively, no implicit story is needed: أن يعلمه is raised by تكن, with feminine agreement because that clause means the sign; the source compares semantic agreement in other verses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p369/r3.anchor: ولا يمتنع أن لا يضمر القصة ولكن يرتفع (أن يعلم) بقوله: (تكن)

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p268#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p268#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p268#2/r1.claim: With yāʾ in يكن and accusative آية, آية is the predicate and أن يعلمه the subject, since the latter means the scholars' knowledge and is definite.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p268#2/r1.anchor: والحجة لمن نصب أنه جعل الآية الخبر والاسم أن يعلمه لأنه بمعنى علم علماء بني إسرائيل فهو أولى بالاسم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p268#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p268#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p268#2/r2.claim: With tāʾ and nominative آية, آية is the subject of kāna and أن يعلمه its predicate.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p268#2/r2.anchor: فالحجة لمن رفع الآية أنه جعلها اسم كان والخبر أن يعلمه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r1.claim: The source dates al-Ḥarra to fifty-three years after the Prophet’s death.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r1.anchor: وكانت الحرة بعد وفاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بثلاث وخمسين سنة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r2.speaker: نافع بن أبي نعيم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r2.claim: After Abū Jaʿfar died, those washing him saw a page-like mark between his neck and heart and took it as the light of the Qurʾān.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r2.anchor: عن نافع بن أبي نعيم قال لما غسل أبو جعفر يزيد بن القعقاع القارىء بعد وفاته

IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r3.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r3.claim: Shayba b. Niṣāḥ was a client of Umm Salama, had met ʿĀʾisha and Umm Salama, and married Abū Jaʿfar’s daughter.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r3.anchor: ومنهم شيبة بن نصاح بن سرجس بن يعقوب مولى أم سلمة رضي الله تعالى عنها زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان قد أدرك عائشة وأم سلمة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r4.speaker: يعقوب بن جعفر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb says Shayba and Abū Jaʿfar taught recitation in the Prophet’s Mosque before al-Ḥarra; Shayba had met ʿĀʾisha, who prayed God would teach him Qurʾān.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r4.anchor: قال كان شيبة وأبو جعفر يقرئان في مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل الحرة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r5.speaker: سليمان بن مسلم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r5.claim: Sulaymān b. Muslim reports that Shayba said he was brought as a child to Umm Salama, who rubbed his head and blessed him.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r5.anchor: قال حدثنا إسماعيل بن جعفر بن أبي كثير قال أخبرني سليمان بن مسلم أن شيبة أخبره أنه أتى به وهو صغير إلى أم سلمة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r6.claim: When questioned about marrying his poor daughter to Shayba despite wealthier suitors, Abū Jaʿfar replied that Shayba would fill her house with Qurʾān.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r6.anchor: فقيل لأبي جعفر زوجت ابنتك شيبة وهو مقل وقد كان يرغب فيها سروات الموالي قال فقال أبو جعفر إن كان شيبة مقلا فسيملأ بيتها قرآنا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r7.speaker: الناس
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r7.claim: People said a muṣḥaf would be born from Shayba and Abū Jaʿfar’s daughter.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r8.speaker: المفضل بن غسان
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r8.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal b. Ghassān reports that Shayba led the funeral prayer for Sukayna, daughter of al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r8.anchor: سمعت المفضل بن غسان الغلابي يقول قدم شيبة بن نصاح فصلى على سكينة ابنة الحسين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r9.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r9.claim: Muslim b. Jundab al-Hudhalī reported from al-Zubayr and Ibn ʿUmar, was eloquent, and preached in Medina.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p58/r9.anchor: ومنهم مسلم بن جندب الهذلي روى عن الزبير بن العوام وابن عمر وكان من فصحاء الناس وكان يقص بالمدينة

NASHR:v2p206/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p206/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p206/r1.claim: Teachers marked unfamiliar passages in a student’s copy, then tested them individually at the request for authorization; failure meant repeating the full reading and test.
NASHR:v2p206/r1.anchor: فإن عرفها أجازه وإلا تركه يجمع ختمة أخرى ويفعل معه كما فعل أولا

NASHR:v2p206/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p206/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p206/r2.claim: This method reflected teachers’ care to transmit knowledge and encourage students to advance and learn more.
NASHR:v2p206/r2.anchor: وذلك كله حرص منهم على الإفادة وتحريض للطالب على الترقي والزيادة

NASHR:v2p206/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p206/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASHR:v2p206/r3.claim: A report in the Ṣaḥīḥ recounts that the Prophet repeatedly told a man whose prayer was inadequate to pray again, then taught him how to pray.
NASHR:v2p206/r3.anchor: ففي الصحيح أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - دخل المسجد فدخل رجل فصلى

NASHR:v2p206/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p206/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p206/r4.claim: The Prophet could have taught the man immediately, but delayed instruction to draw attention to the lesson and make it firmer in memory.
NASHR:v2p206/r4.anchor: ويكون أرسخ في حفظه وأبلغ في ذكره

QIRAAT-ER:26:197:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:26:197:3#1/r1.claim: The segment labels yakun the canonical reading.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p76#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p76#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p76#3/r1.claim: Qatada says the Prophet himself was a sign for them: Israel’s scholars knew him because they found him described in their scriptures.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p76#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ أو لم يكن لهم آية أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل ﴾ قال ألم يكن لهم النبي آية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r1.claim: The hamza can seek confirmation or express denial and negation; the waw coordinates with an omitted clause implied by the context, such as asking whether they overlooked the sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r1.anchor: الهمزة للتقرير أو للانكار والنفي والواو للعطف على مقدر يقتضيه المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r2.claim: لهم is attached to the verb of being and moved before its subject أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل, foregrounding the sign that Quran's described qualities are known from their books.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r2.anchor: على أن ( لهم ) متعلق بالكون قدم على اسمه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r3.claim: Al-Alusi takes the object pronoun as referring to the Quran, whose features were described in the Israelites' scriptures.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r3.anchor: القرءان بنعوته المذ : ورة في كتبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r4.claim: Qatada takes the pronoun to refer to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r4.anchor: وعن قتادة أن الضمير للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r5.claim: Another view takes the pronoun as referring to the preceding statement that the Quran is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, brought by the faithful Spirit to Muhammad; Al-Alusi considers this remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r5.anchor: وقيل : العلم على معناه المشهور والضمير للحكم السابق في قوله تعالى ( وإنه لتنزيل رب العالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r6.claim: Al-Tha'labi reports from Ibn Abbas that Meccans asked the Jewish scholars of Yathrib about the Prophet; they said it was his time and described him, but mixed up what they said about Muhammad. The verse was revealed on that occasion.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r6.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي عن ابن عباس أن أهل مكة بعثوا إلى أحبار يثرب يسألونهم عن النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r7.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r7.claim: Muqatil says this verse is Medinan; Al-Alusi notes that the occasion report and the verse's context support its being Meccan.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل : هي مدنية وعلماء بني إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify the scholars as converts such as Abdullah ibn Salam, who pointed out passages in the Torah and Gospel describing the Messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r8.anchor: وعلماء بني إسرائيل عبد الله بن سلام ونحوه كما روي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r9.claim: Other views include all Israelite scholars, whether Muslim or not, or their prophets, who had alerted people to the Prophet; Al-Alusi says the prophets reading is not apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r9.anchor: وقيل : علماؤهم من أسلم منهم ومن لم يسلم وقيل : انبياؤهم فانهم نبهوا على ذلك وهو خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r10.claim: Al-Alusi prefers contemporary scholars of the two scriptural communities, whether Muslim or not.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r10.anchor: ولعل أظهر الأقوال كون المراد به معاصريه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من علماء أهل الكتابين المسلمين وغيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r11.speaker: ابن عامر والجحدري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r11.claim: Ibn Amir and al-Jahdari read تكن with feminine agreement and آية nominative, treating آية as the subject of تكن and the أن-clause as predicate; Al-Alusi notes the predicate order is grammatically weak and gives alternative analyses through an omitted predicate or a clause-of-state subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر والجحدري ( تكن ) بالتأنيث وءاية بالرفع وجعلت اسم تكن وأن يعلمه خبرها وضعف

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas reads feminine تكن with آية in the accusative, like the feminine verb and accusative predicate in 6:23; Al-Alusi explains feminine agreement by construing the subject phrase as a feminine expression, and rejects deriving it from the genitive noun as lacking the usual condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( تكن ) بالتأنيث وءاية بالنصب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r13.speaker: لبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r13.claim: Labid's verse about a wild ass and she-ass supplies a poetic parallel for feminine agreement with the predicative expression, as in the variant construction here.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r13.anchor: فمضى وقدمها وكانت عادة منه إذا هي عردت اقدامها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r14.speaker: الجحدري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r14.claim: Al-Jahdari reads تعلمه with feminine agreement, taking the subject to be the collective body of Israelite scholars.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r14.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري تعلمه بالتأنيث على أن المراد جماعة علماء بني إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r15.claim: The Quran manuscript spells علماء with a wāw between mīm and alif, explained as an orthographic trace of a dialect that changes the alif of علماء to wāw, as in الصلاة and الزكاة.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p126/r15.anchor: وكتب في المصحف علمؤا بواو بين الميم والألف ووجه ذلك بانه على لغة من يميل الف علماء إلى الواو

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads تكن with آية nominative, making آية the subject and أن يعلمه its predicate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر: "تكن" بالتاء "آية" بالرفع، جعل الآية اسما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r4.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r4.claim: The other readers use masculine يكن and accusative آية, making Israelite scholars’ knowledge the sign for the deniers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r4.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالياء، "آية"] (1) نصب، جعلوا الآية خبر يكن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r5.claim: The sign is that Israelite scholars knew Muhammad’s prophethood because they reported his mention in their books; they included ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r5.anchor: لأن العلماء الذين كانوا من بني إسرائيل، كانوا يخبرون بوجود ذكره في كتبهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Meccans asked the Jews in Medina, who said Muhammad’s time had come and his description was in the Torah, confirming his truth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بعث أهل مكة إلى اليهود وهم بالمدينة فسألوهم عن محمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129#2/r1.speaker: عطية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129#2/r1.claim: ʿAtiyya identifies the Israelite scholars as five: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, Ibn Yamin, Thaʿlaba, Asad, and Usayd.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129#2/r1.anchor: قال عطية: كانوا خمسة عبد الله بن سلام، وابن يامين، وثعلبة، وأسد، وأسيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r4.claim: Israelite scholars' knowledge is a sign of the Qur'an's truth or Muhammad's prophethood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r4.anchor: على صحة القرآن أو نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r5.claim: Israelite scholars recognize the Qur'an from descriptions in their books, establishing it as evidence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r5.anchor: أن يعرفوه بنعته المذكور في كتبهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads takun with feminine agreement and āyatun in the nominative.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر تكن بالتاء و { ءاية } بالرفع

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r7.claim: On this reading āyah may be the subject with lahum as predicate and an yaʿlamahu an appositive or agent; alternatively it may be a pronoun-of-affair construction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r7.anchor: على أنها الاسم والخبر { لهم } { وأن يعلمه } بدل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r9.claim: In the majority reading, the predicate comes before the subject: ‘a sign’ is accusative, followed by the explanatory clause that Israel’s scholars know it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r9.anchor: اقتضى تقديم الخبر على الاسم في قراءة الجمهور بالتذكير والنصب , فقال بعد تقديم لما اقتضاه من الحال : { آية } أي علامة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r10.speaker: ابن عامر
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r10.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the verb as feminine and raises ‘sign’ as the subject, with the clause about Israel’s scholars knowing it as predicate.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r10.anchor: وأنث ابن عامر الفعل ورفع { آية } اسما وأخبر عنها بأن والفعل { علماء بني إسرائيل * }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r11.claim: Israelite scholars’ recognition is proof because Quraysh often relied on them for religious reports; their scriptures describe the Prophet, and many accepted Islam.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r11.anchor: فإن قريشا كانوا كثيرا ما يرجعون إليهم ويعولون في الأخبار الإلهية عليهم , فإن كثيرا منهم أسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r12.claim: The Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and other prophetic books confirm the Qur’an and the Prophet’s attributes; their later alteration does not erase their evidentiary force for their adherents.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r12.anchor: وذكر تصديق التوارة والإنجيل والزبور وغيرها من أسفار الأنبياء عليهم السلام للقرآن في صفة النبي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r13.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Meccans asked Jews about Muhammad; they replied that his time had come and that the Torah described him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r13.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن أهل مكة بعثوا إلى اليهود يسألونهم عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا : هذا زمانه , وإنا لنجد في التوراة صفته

DURR-FULL:v6p321/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r7.claim: Qatāda says Jews and Christians knew that Muhammad was identified in their Torah and Gospel as God’s Messenger.
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وإنه لفي زبر الأولين} قال: كتب الأولين {أو لم يكن لهم آية

DURR-FULL:v6p322/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r1.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim read the verb in the phrase with yāʾ.
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r1.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ (أو لم يكن لهم آية) بالياء

DURR-FULL:v6p322/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the Israelite scholars as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and other learned men.
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أو لم يكن لهم آية أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل} قال: عبد الله بن سلام وغيره من علمائهم

DURR-FULL:v6p322/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām was one of the best Israelite scholars, accepted Muhammad’s Book, and served as a sign of their scholars’ knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان عبد الله بن سلام من علماء بني إسرائيل وكان من خيارهم فآمن بكتاب محمد

DURR-FULL:v6p322/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r4.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد القرشي
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r4.claim: Mubashshir ibn ʿUbayd al-Qurashī says the Qurʾān itself is the sign.
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r4.anchor: عن مبشر بن عبيد القرشي في قوله {أو لم يكن لهم آية} يقول: أو لم يكن لهم القرآن آية

DURR-FULL:v6p322/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r5.speaker: عطية العوفي
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r5.claim: ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī says the Israelite scholars were five: Asad, Asīd, Ibn Yāmīn, Thaʿlaba, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.
DURR-FULL:v6p322/r5.anchor: عن عطية العوفي في قوله {أو لم يكن لهم آية أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل} قال: كانوا خمسة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r1.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r1.claim: Mubashshir interprets the sign as the Quran itself.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r1.anchor: مبشر بن عبيد القرشي قراءة : اولم يكن لهم آية يقول : اولم يكن لهم القران آية

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the Prophet himself was the sign for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : أو لم يكن لهم آية قال : لم يكن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آية

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the Israelite scholars as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and other learned men among them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : علماء بني اسرائيل عبد الله بن سلام وغيره من علمائهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r4.speaker: عطية
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r4.claim: ʿAṭiyya names five Israelite scholars: Asad, Asīd, Ibn Yāmīn, Thaʿlaba, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r4.anchor: عن عطية اولم يكن لهم آية ان يعلمه علماء بني اسرائيل قال : كانوا خمسة اسد ، واسيد ، وابن يامين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r5.claim: Qatada says Jews and Christians knew that Muhammad was written about in the Torah and Gospel as God's Messenger.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : اولم يكن لهم آية ان يعلمه علماء بني اسرائيل يعني : بذلك اليهود والنصارى انهم يجدون محمدا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām was among the best of the Israelite scholars and believed in Muhammad's Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : اولم يكن لهم آية ان يعلمه علماء بني اسرائيل قال : كان عبد الله بن سلام من علماء بني اسرائيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r1.claim: This is a third commendation of the Qur’an: Israelite scholars’ recognition is evidence supporting the preceding commendation, that earlier prophetic books attest to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r1.anchor: تنويه ثالث بالقرآن وحجة على التنويه الثاني به الذي هو شهادة كتب الأنبياء له بالصدق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r2.claim: Because the clause is also a new commendation, it is coordinated with the preceding statement; if it served only as evidence, coordination would not be expected.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r2.anchor: فباعتبار كون هذه الجملة تنويها آخر بالقرآن عطفت على الجملة التي قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r3.claim: Their knowing includes recognizing the Qur’an’s qualities and verifying that its bearer truly has those qualities, as well as knowing what it contains from their scriptures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r3.anchor: وفعل : { يعلمه } شامل للعلم بصفة القرآن ، أي تحقق صدق الصفات الموصوف بها من جاء به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r4.claim: The pronoun may refer to the Qur’an, with the sense ‘know its mention,’ or to the previously stated fact that it is in earlier writings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p192/r4.anchor: وضمير { أن يعلمه } عائد إلى القرآن على تقدير : أن يعلم ذكره . ويجوز أن يعود على الحكم المذكور

BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r3.claim: The hamza denies a negative; the waw coordinates with an omitted clause, لهم is circumstantial, and the pronoun refers to Quraysh. آية precedes its subject for emphasis.
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r3.anchor: الهمزة لإنكار النفي والواو للعطف على مقدر ولهم حال من آية والضمير راجع إلى مشركي قريش

BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r4.claim: Israelite scholars such as Abdullah ibn Salam knew the Qur'an's described traits from their books, making their knowledge a sign of the Qur'an's divine origin and the Messenger's truth.
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r4.anchor: كعبد الله ن سلام ونحوه بنعوته المذكورة في كتبهم ويعلموا من أنزل عليه

BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r5.claim: Meccans asked Jews of Medina about Muhammad and his mission; they replied that it was his time and the Torah described him.
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r5.anchor: مكة بعثوا إلى يهود المدينة يسألونهم عن محمد وبعثته فقالوا : إن هذا لزمانه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p224/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p224/r1.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p224/r1.claim: The majority say the whole sura is Meccan; Muqatil says the verse mentioning the poets is Medinan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p224/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كلها فيما قال جمهور الناس، وقال مقاتل منها مدني الآية التي تذكر فيها الشعراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r13.claim: Israelite scholars such as Abdullah ibn Salam knowing the Qur'an should have confirmed its truth to the Meccans.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r13.anchor: كون علماء بني إسرائيل يعلمونه كعبد الله بن سلام ونحوه قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas, as cited by al-Thaʿlabi, says Meccans asked Yathrib's rabbis about the Prophet; they described his time and qualities, then became confused about Muhammad, prompting the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا فيما حكى عنه الثعلبي أن أهل مكة بعثوا إلى الأحبار بيثرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r1.claim: He regards the verse as Meccan, supporting the view that Israelite scholars had the Torah's description of the unlettered Prophet; Muqatil calls it Medinan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: ويؤيد هذا كون الآية مكية، وقال مقاتل هذه الآية مدنية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم الجحدري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r2.claim: Unlike the others' masculine يكن with accusative آية, they read feminine تكن with nominative آية.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r2.anchor: وكلهم قرأ يكن بالياء آية نصبا غير ابن عامر فإنه قرأ «تكن» بالتاء من فوق «آية» رفعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r3.speaker: الجحدري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r3.claim: Al-Jahdari reads تعلمه with feminine ت instead of the majority's masculine ي.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r3.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «أن يعلمه» بالياء من تحت، وقرأ الجحدري «تعلمه» بالتاء من فوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r11.speaker: الجمهور وابن مسعود والأعمش وأبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r11.claim: Most read masculine يكن with accusative آية; Ibn Masud and al-Aʿmash have another wording, and Ubay's codex omits the opening waw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r11.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «أو لم يكن» بالياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r12.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r12.claim: A group reads feminine تكن with nominative آية; some readers of masculine يكن use accusative آية and the rest nominative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p243/r12.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «تكن» بالتاء من فوق «آية» رفعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r1.claim: These readers use masculine yakun and put āyatan in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي أو لم يكن لهم بالياء آية بالنصب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r2.claim: With masculine yakun, āyatan is best read as the predicate, and the clause an yaʿlamahu is the subject: their scholars' knowledge is a sign.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج إذا قلت يكن بالياء فالاختيار نصب آية ويكون أن اسم كان ويكون آية خبر كان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAmir and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read feminine takun and āyatun in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وابن أبي عبلة تكن بالتاء آية بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r4.claim: With feminine takun and nominative āyatun, āya is the subject and an yaʿlamahu the predicate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ أو لم تكن بالتاء آية جعل آية هي الاسم وأن يعلمه خبر تكن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r5.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r5.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni and Qatada read feminine takun with āyatan in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمران الجوني وقتادة تكن بالتاء آية بالنصب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows the feminine construction with accusative āyatan by analogy with 6:23, where their trial is not.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r6.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أو لم تكن بالتاء آية بالنصب كقوله ثم لم تكن فتنتهم الأنعام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r7.speaker: الشعبي والضحاك وعاصم الجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r7.claim: These readers pronounce the verb with tāʾ: an taʿlamahu.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r7.anchor: وقرأ الشعبي والضحاك وعاصم الجحدري أن تعلمه بالتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r8.claim: The sign is the knowledge of Israelite scholars that Muhammad and his prophethood are true, since they found his description in the Torah and Gospel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r8.anchor: المعنى أو لم يكن لهم علم علماء بني إسرائيل أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حق وأن نبوته حق آية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says Meccans asked the Jews in Medina about Muhammad, and they confirmed that his time had come and that the Torah described him; this was a sign of his truth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#4/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس بعث أهل مكة إلى اليهود وهم بالمدينة يسألونهم عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا إن هذا لزمانه

JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads feminine takun and nominative āyatun, making the sign the subject.
JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر: أولم تكن بالتاء آية بالرفع،

JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r2.claim: Others read masculine yakun and accusative āyatan; the pronoun means scholars' knowledge, subject to the sign's predicate.
JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالياء، آية بالنصب، فعلى هذا الهاء كناية عن علم علماء بني إسرائيل،

MUJAHID:v2p466/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p466/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p466/r1.claim: The Israelite scholars who knew the Quran include Abdullah ibn Salam and other scholars who became Muslim.
MUJAHID:v2p466/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل ﴾ يعني عبد الله بن سلام وغيره من علمائهم

MUQATIL:26:190-200/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:190-200/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:190-200/r9.claim: The sign for Meccans is that the scholars of the Children of Israel, including Ibn Salam and his companions, know of Muhammad.
MUQATIL:26:190-200/r9.anchor: أو لم يكن } محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { لهم آية } يعنى لكفار مكة { أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.speaker: الشامي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.claim: The Shami reading makes ayatan the subject of kana and the clause that scholars know it the predicate.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.anchor: شامى جعلت آية اسم كان وخبره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.claim: Other parses make takun contain an implicit affair-pronoun, ayatan the fronted predicate, and the knowledge clause its subject; or take kana as complete, with ayatan its subject.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.anchor: وقيل فى تكن ضمير القصة وآية خبر مقدم والمبتدأ أن يعلمه والجملة خبر كان وقيل كان تامة والفاعل آية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.claim: The sign is that Israelite scholars such as Abdullah ibn Salam know the Quran from its mention in the Torah; the passage quotes their affirmation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.anchor: كعبد الله بن سلام وغيره قال الله تعالى وإذا يتلى عليهم قالوا آمنا به

NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.claim: The Quranic manuscript spelling writes scholars with a waw before the alif.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.anchor: وخط فى المصحف علمؤا بواو قبل الألف

QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r1.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r1.claim: Mujāhid identifies the Israelite scholars as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, Salmān, and other converts.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني عبد الله بن سلام وسلمان وغيرهما ممن أسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Meccans consulted the Jews in Medina about Muḥammad; they said his time had arrived and his description was in the Torah.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: بعث أهل مكة إلى اليهود وهم بالمدينة يسألونهم عن محمد عليه السلام، فقالوا: إن هذا لزمانه، وإنا لنجد في التوراة نعته وصفته.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r3.claim: On this explanation, the wording includes anyone knowledgeable about Jewish scripture, whether or not that person converted.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r3.anchor: فيرجع لفظ العلماء إلى كل من كان له علم بكتبهم أسلم أو لم يسلم على هذا القول.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r4.claim: Their testimony convinced the polytheists because they consulted the People of the Book for religious knowledge and presumed them learned.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r4.anchor: وإنما صارت شهادة أهل الكتاب حجة على المشركين لأنهم كانوا يرجعون في أشياء من أمور الدين إلى أهل الكتاب لأنهم مظنون بهم علم.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r5.speaker: ابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads takūna with a feminine subject āya and the scholars' clause as predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر { أولم تكن لهم آية }. الباقون { أولم يكن لهم آية }

QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r6.claim: In the majority reading, an yaʿlamahu is the subject of yakun and āyatan its accusative predicate: the scholars' knowledge is a clear sign.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r6.anchor: الباقون { أولم يكن لهم آية } بالنصب على الخبر واسم يكن { أن يعلمه } والتقدير أولم يكن لهم علم علماء بني إسرائيل الذين أسلموا آية واضحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r7.speaker: عاصم الجحدري
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r7.claim: ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī reads taʿlamahu with the feminine verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:197-201/r7.anchor: وقرأ عاصم الجحدري { أن تعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل }.

STUDYQURAN:26:197/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:197/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:26:197/r1.claim: Q and Ṭ identify the learned among the Children of Israel with figures including ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, a learned Madinan Jew whose conversion mattered because of his standing.
STUDYQURAN:26:197/r1.anchor: because of his knowledge and standing within the Jewish community of his time, of special significance (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:26:197/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:197/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:197/r2.claim: That identification conflicts with the sūra's Makkan dating because Ibn Salām converted only after the Prophet's migration to Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:26:197/r2.anchor: would not harmonize with the opinion that this sūrah is from the Makkan period

STUDYQURAN:26:197/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:197/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:26:197/r3.claim: Q says Makkan idolaters consulted People of the Book, and at least some said Muhammad was the prophet described in their scriptures and that his time had come.
STUDYQURAN:26:197/r3.anchor: were told by at least some of them that he was the prophet described in their scriptures and that this was his time (Q)

TAB-FULL:v17p644/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p644/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p644/r1.claim: The broad wording 'earlier scriptures' is general in form but specific in scope: the Qur'an and its news are found in some scriptures revealed to some messengers.
TAB-FULL:v17p644/r1.anchor: وإن هذا القرآن لفي زبر الأولين: يعني في كتب الأولين، وخرج مخرج العموم ومعناه الخصوص

TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r1.claim: The Israelites’ scholars knowing the Quran’s truth and soundness is a sign to the rejecters that Muhammad is the Lord of the Worlds’ messenger.
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r1.anchor: {أولم يكن لهم آية أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل} [الشعراء: 197]

TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Abdullah ibn Salam, one of Israel’s best scholars who believed Muhammad’s Book, as the sign meant here.
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {أولم يكن لهم آية أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل} [الشعراء: 197] قال: " كان عبد الله بن سلام

TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r3.claim: Mujahid names Abdullah ibn Salam and other Israelite scholars as the scholars referred to.
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {علماء بني إسرائيل} [الشعراء: 197] قال: «عبد الله بن سلام وغيره من علمائهم»

TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the sign as Muhammad being recognized by the Israelite scholars.
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج: " {أولم يكن لهم آية} [الشعراء: 197] ، قال محمد: {أن يعلمه} [الشعراء: 197] قال: يعرفه

TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r5.claim: Qatada says Israel’s scholars knew Muhammad was written about in their scripture.
TAB-FULL:v17p644#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {أولم يكن لهم آية أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل} [الشعراء: 197] ، قال: «أولم يكن للنبي آية، علامة

TABATABAI:26:194-197/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:194-197/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:194-197/r8.claim: Jewish scholars’ knowledge of earlier scriptural predictions about the Qur’an or its revelation to Muhammad is a sign for polytheists confirming his prophethood; Jews used it to give glad tidings and seek advantage over Arabs.
TABATABAI:26:194-197/r8.anchor: أي أولم يكن علم علماء بني إسرائيل بخبر القرآن أو نزوله عليك على سبيل البشارة في كتب الأنبياء الماضين آية للمشركين

TABRISI:26:192-212/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:192-212/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
TABRISI:26:192-212/r2.claim: Ibn Amir reads the verb with feminine tāʾ and āya in the nominative; the other readers use masculine yāʾ and put āya in the accusative.
TABRISI:26:192-212/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر أو لم تكن بالتاء آية بالرفع والباقون لم يكن بالياء آية بالنصب

TABRISI:26:192-212/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:192-212/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:26:192-212/r5.claim: Abu Ali explains feminine takun by an implicit story pronoun interpreted by the following clause; alternatively, the clause أن يعلمه itself is the feminine āya in meaning.
TABRISI:26:192-212/r5.anchor: والوجه في قراءة ابن عامر أو لم تكن لهم آية إن في تكن ضمير القصة والحديث

TABRISI:26:192-196/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:192-196/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:192-196/r18.claim: Israelite scholars' knowledge that the Quran's coming had been foretold in their scriptures is evidence for Muhammad's prophethood.
TABRISI:26:192-196/r18.anchor: معناه أولم يكن لهم علم علماء بني إسرائيل بمجيئه على ما تقدمت البشارة دلالة لهم على صحة نبوته

TABRISI:26:192-196/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:192-196/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:26:192-196/r19.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the Israelite scholars as Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions; their reports helped convert the Aws and Khazraj.
TABRISI:26:192-196/r19.anchor: وعلماء بني إسرائيل عبد الله بن سلام وأصحابه عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:26:192-196/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:192-196/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:192-196/r20.claim: Israelites told Arabs of the Quran's mention in their books and foretold the Prophet, which contributed to the conversion of Aws and Khazraj.
TABRISI:26:192-196/r20.anchor: وكانت اليهود تبشر به وتستفتح على العرب به وكان ذلك سبب إسلام الأوس والخزرج

THALABI:v7p179/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p179/r7.speaker: ابن عامر
THALABI:v7p179/r7.claim: Ibn Amir reads ayatan in the nominative, while the other readers put it in the accusative.
THALABI:v7p179/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر تكن بالتاء آية بالرفع، غيره تكن بالتاء آية بالنصب

THALABI:v7p179/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p179/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p179/r8.claim: The verse asks whether it is not a sign for the deniers that scholars of the Children of Israel recognize Muhammad.
THALABI:v7p179/r8.anchor: ومعنى الآية أو لم يكن لهؤلاء المنكرين دلالة وعلامة أن يعلمه يعني محمدا علماء بني إسرائيل

THALABI:v7p179/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p179/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p179/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Meccans asked Jews in Medina about Muhammad; they said his time had come and that the Torah described him, which was a sign of his truthfulness.
THALABI:v7p179/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بعث أهل مكة الى اليهود وهم بالمدينة فسألوهم عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: إن هذا لزمانه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p126/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p126/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p126/r1.claim: One parse raises āya as the predicate of the clause whose subject is that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p126/r1.anchor: (ءاية) مرتفعة بأنها خبر الابتداء الذي هو: {أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p126/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p126/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p126/r2.claim: Alternatively, no implicit clause is needed: أن يعلمه is raised by تكن, feminine because its meaning is āya; agreement by meaning is illustrated by 6:160 and a recitation of 6:23.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p126/r2.anchor: ولكن ترفع: {أن يعلمه} بقوله: (تكن) وإن كان في تكن علامة تأنيث؛

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:196-197/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:196-197/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:196-197/r2.claim: For the polytheists, a sign of Muhammad's truth is that the scholars of the Children of Israel know him as prophet and messenger.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:196-197/r2.anchor: دلالة على صدقه { أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل } يعلمون محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم بالنبوة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r8.claim: The phrase is read with either tāʾ or yāʾ: the tāʾ reading says they had a sign; the yāʾ reading treats “their having a sign” as the subject of “was.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r8.anchor: قال: {أولم يكن لهم آية} [الشعراء: 197] وهي تقرأ على وجهين، بالتاء والياء، فمن قرأها بالتاء يقول: قد كانت لهم آية

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r1.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the scholars of the Children of Israel means those among them who believed; their belief in Muhammad is a sign.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r1.anchor: يعني: من آمن منهم، أي: فقد كان لهم في إيمانهم به آية، هذا تفسير الحسن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r2.claim: Qatadah says the Jews and Christians find in the Torah and Gospel that Muhammad is God's Messenger.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: يعني: اليهود والنصارى أنهم يجدون محمدا في التوراة والإنجيل أنه رسول الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r3.speaker: ابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r3.claim: Ibn Mujahid, from his father, names Abdullah ibn Salam and other learned Israelites among them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p524/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: منهم عبد الله بن سلام، وغيره من علمائهم.

ELMALILI:26:192-209/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:192-209/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:192-209/r9.claim: Some Israelite scholars said the Prophet's attributes and description appear in the Torah and Gospel, and Quraysh went to them to learn this report.
ELMALILI:26:192-209/r9.anchor: Benî İsrâil ulemâsından bir kısmı Tevrat ve İncil’de Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm’ın

ELMALILI:26:192-209/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:192-209/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:192-209/r10.claim: The Israelite scholars' recognition of the Quran is itself a sign for those who deny it.
ELMALILI:26:192-209/r10.anchor: Benî İsrâil ulemâsının onu bilmesi bile onu inkâr edenlere bir delil değil midir?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r4.speaker: bir kısım müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r4.claim: Some exegetes identify the Israelite scholars as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and other Jewish scholars who became Muslim.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r4.anchor: Bir kısım müfessirler “İsrâiloğulları bilginleri”nden maksadın Abdullah b. Selâm ve onun gibi müslüman olan bazı yahudi bilginleri olduğunu söylemişlerse de

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r5.claim: The author prefers the general referent: Jewish scholars whether or not they had become Muslim.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r5.anchor: âyeti genel anlamda –müslüman olsun olmasın– yahudi bilginleri olarak değerlendirmek daha uygundur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r6.speaker: Kurtubî, Ebû Hayyân
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r6.claim: According to a report, Meccans sent someone to Jewish scholars in Medina to ask about Muhammad; they replied that a prophet of this kind would come and that the Torah described his qualities.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r6.anchor: Rivayete göre Mekkeliler Medine’de bulunan yahudi bilginlerine adam gönderip Hz. Peygamber’in durumu hakkında onlardan bilgi istemişler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r7.claim: Some Israelite scholars in the Meccan period acknowledged that Qur'anic accounts of earlier peoples agreed with those in the Torah.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r7.anchor: Özellikle Mekke döneminde, İsrâiloğulları bilginlerinden bazıları Kur’an’da anlatılan bu kıssaların Tevrat’ta anlatılanlara uygun olduğu gerçeğini teslim ediyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r8.claim: Ankebût 29:47 reports that some People of the Book believed in the Qur'an, supporting this point about earlier Jewish scholars.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r8.anchor: Mekke döneminde inmiş olan Ankebût sûresinin 47. âyetinde Ehl-i kitap’tan bazılarının Kur’an’a iman ettikleri haber verilmiştir

BURHAN:v1p36/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p36/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن الشهرابانى
BURHAN:v1p36/r1.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Shahrabānī says Abū Bakr al-Naysābūrī first made the study of textual correspondence prominent in Baghdad, asking why verses and sūras are placed beside one another.
BURHAN:v1p36/r1.anchor: وقال الشيخ أبو الحسن الشهرابانى أول من أظهر ببغداد علم المناسبة ولم نكن سمعناه من غيره هو الشيخ الإمام أبو بكر النيسابورى

BURHAN:v1p36/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p36/r2.speaker: عز الدين بن عبد السلام
BURHAN:v1p36/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām says correspondence is useful when a discourse has one connected subject, but insisting on links among revelations with different causes and rulings is strained.
BURHAN:v1p36/r2.anchor: وقال الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام المناسبة علم حسن ولكن يشترط في حسن ارتباط الكلام أن يقع في أمر متحد مرتبط أوله بآخره

BURHAN:v1p36/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p36/r3.speaker: بعض مشايخنا المحققين
BURHAN:v1p36/r3.claim: Some exacting scholars answer that revelation followed events while the muṣḥaf order follows wisdom and prophetic instruction, matching the heavenly archetype; its arrangement is part of its manifest inimitability.
BURHAN:v1p36/r3.anchor: قال بعض مشايخنا المحققين قد وهم من قال لا يطلب للآي الكريمة مناسبة لأنها حسب الوقائع المتفرقة وفصل الخطاب أنها على حسب الوقائع تنزيلا وعلى حسب الحكمة ترتيبا

BURHAN:v1p36/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p36/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p36/r4.claim: The method is first to decide whether a verse completes the preceding one or stands independently; if independent, ask how it relates to what came before, and apply the same inquiry to sūras.
BURHAN:v1p36/r4.anchor: والذي ينبغي في كل آية أن يبحث أول كل شيء عن كونها مكملة لما قبلها أو مستقلة ثم المستقلة ما وجه مناسبتها لما قبلها

ITQAN:v3p289/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p289/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p289/r1.claim: Revelation came in response to events, while the Quran’s order follows wisdom; its suras and verses were arranged by prophetic instruction as they were revealed to the lowest heaven, and their arrangement is a clear miracle.
ITQAN:v3p289/r1.anchor: وفصل الخطاب أنها على حسب الوقائع تنزيلا وعلى حسب الحكمة ترتيبا وتأصيلا فالمصحف على وفق ما في اللوح المحفوظ مرتبة سوره كلها وآياته بالتوقيف

ITQAN:v3p289/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p289/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p289/r2.claim: For each verse, first ask whether it completes the preceding verse or stands independently, then examine its connection; do the same for each sura and its purpose.
ITQAN:v3p289/r2.anchor: والذي ينبغي في كل آية أن يبحث أول كل شيء عن كونها مكملة لما قبلها أو مستقلة ثم المستقلة ما وجه مناسبتها لما قبلها

ITQAN:v3p289/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p289/r3.speaker: الرازي
ITQAN:v3p289/r3.claim: Al-Razi says the Quran’s arrangement and ordering, alongside its eloquence and meanings, are miraculous; he faults most exegetes for overlooking the subtleties of this order.
ITQAN:v3p289/r3.anchor: وقال الإمام الرازي في سورة البقرة ومن تأمل في لطائف نظم هذه السورة وفي بدائع ترتيبها علم أن القرآن كما أنه معجز

ITQAN:v4p424/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p424/r1.speaker: ابن عبد البر
ITQAN:v4p424/r1.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr calls the two preceding authorities imams of the Sunna and comments that neither took a position in this issue; the excerpt does not identify them.
ITQAN:v4p424/r1.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر فهذان إمامان بالسنة ما قاما ولا قعدا في هذه المسألة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r1.claim: Thought cannot engage individual word meanings stripped of syntax: a verb is considered with a noun to govern, and a noun with a grammatical role such as subject, object, predicate, or modifier.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r1.anchor: لا يتصور أن يتعلق الفكر بمعاني الكلم أفرادا ومجردة من معاني النحو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r2.claim: Reordering قفا نبك into an arrangement that blocks grammatical relations leaves the reader unable to connect thought to any word's meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r2.anchor: من نبك قفا حبيب ذكرى منزل ' ، ثم انظر هل يتعلق منك فكر بمعنى كلمة منها ؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r3.claim: He clarifies that thought can compare lexical meanings, but only after assigning the words syntactic functions suited to praise, blame, simile, or another aim.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r3.anchor: واعلم أني لست أقول إن الفكر لا يتعلق بمعاني الكلم المفردة أصلا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r4.claim: Bishr's simile shows that each phrase is conceived through its grammatical relation: annexation, attachment, coordination, predicate, and the clause describing the night.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303#2/r4.anchor: فخذ بيت بشار ، + الطويل + : ( كأن مثار النقع فوق رؤوسنا وأسيافنا ليل تهاوى كواكبه )

BURHAN:v2p410/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p410/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p410/r6.claim: On the cited reading, أن يعلمه is the subject and آية the predicate; the pronoun is a pronoun of affair and is feminine because آية occurs in the sentence.
BURHAN:v2p410/r6.anchor: بقراءة الياء وأن يعلمه بمتدأ وآية الخبر والهاء ضمير القصة وأنث لوجود آية في الكلام

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p447/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p447/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p447/r3.claim: Earlier scriptures predicted the Qur’an, and Israelite scholars know these prophecies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p447/r3.anchor: Previous scriptures have predicted it and the scholars of the Israelites are aware of these prophesies.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p449/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p449/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p449/r8.claim: Earlier scriptures contain prophecies of the Prophet’s advent and call, known to Israelite scholars though concealed by most; some accepted the Qur’an and Muhammad.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p449/r8.anchor: among them were the true scholars too who openly acknowledged the Qur’ ān and also professed faith in Muḥammad (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r1.claim: The cited prophecies and believing Israelite scholars challenge the opponents: the author asks what further proof they require.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r1.anchor: In the above cited verses, these very prophesies and these scholars are referred and the question posed to the opponents of the Qur’ ān. What more do they want.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r2.claim: Arabs considered the People of the Book religiously superior, yet denial blinded them: they treated supportive unbelievers as well-wishers and believers in Muhammad as conspirators.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r2.anchor: in religious issues the Arabs regarded the People of Book to be superior. However, in frenzy of their denial of the Prophet (sws), they had become so blind

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r3.claim: The author says his reading of the verse is clear and has parallels in earlier and later sūrahs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r3.anchor: Its parallels can be seen in the earlier sūrahs as well as in the succeeding ones.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r4.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r4.claim: Some have attributed to the jurists the deduction that the Qur’an may be read in a non-Arabic language.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r4.anchor: some people have ascribed an opinion to our jurists that they have deduced from this verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r5.claim: The author rejects that deduction: a rendering into another language is a translation, not the Qur’an, and no translated verse or sūrah can replace the Arabic original.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r5.anchor: If the Qur’ ān is rendered into another language, it cannot be called the Qur’ ān; it will be its translation and there is great difference between a text and its translation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r6.claim: Even with clear meanings and a capable translator, the Qur’an’s full meaning and eloquence cannot be rendered; translations of other scriptures also cannot replace their originals.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r6.anchor: after years of hard work, when he gets down to translating them, he feels that, in spite of having the ability to translate, he is not able to fully render the verses, let alone their eloquence.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r7.claim: He says Jews and Christians went astray in part because original scriptural languages died out and translations became substitutes grounding their understanding and reasoning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r7.anchor: the major reason for the Jews and Christians going astray is that the original languages of their scriptures became extinct and they regarded their translations to be their substitute.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r8.claim: The author says Saint Paul manipulated translations to lead Christians astray.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r8.anchor: I have already explained at an appropriate instance how Saint Paul manipulated the translations to lead the Christians astray.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r9.claim: He calls the juristic deduction groundless and gravely consequential, suggesting it was attributed to the jurists through misunderstanding.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p450/r9.anchor: I think that this deduction from the verse has no grounds and is totally wrong in itself; in fact, it is a matter of grave consequence
